claims.summary: For h>=1 disjoint live ternary edge pairs, with zero-label indicators x_i,y_i, the real bit function E=x_1 product_i(1+x_i+y_i) evaluated in F2 has exact minimum signed width-one categorical CNF mass 2^(h-1). A rectangle functional attains this lower bound. A complete accuracy-h block on the fixed tuple of all edge-zero indicators can select these pairs after restriction; on the recorded good hard-graph event, K>=0,K+B<=D_H,B>=2h+1 ensures enough live edges and retains original costs. The total companion mass is then at least 2^(h-1) on every good restriction. For any finite fixed row family with width-two companion CNFs, however, expected minimum total mass is <=m/(1-theta), and conditioned on a positive-probability hard event G is <=m/((1-theta)Pr(G)), theta=(3p/(1-p))^2<1. Thus uniform arbitrary-policy transfer fails, while existential mass minimization survives.
claims.assessment: Working all-parameter elementary norm and source-policy proof, medium reviewed. Applies in the existing growing-degree encoding/replay regime. Does not bound binary error rank, refute good optimized choices, or exclude a candidate hard family. The displayed bad source also admits a zero-error choice whenever an input becomes constant one.
claims.rationale: Answers the scheduled post-restriction joint-law test while separating an unnecessary all-policy guarantee from the existential goal endpoint.
claims.next_action: Seek a direct successful-choice certificate or genuine source-sensitive rank estimate; do not sharpen real mass or treat a scalar-only obstruction as excluding polynomial maps.
